title: Connection-Study Report Template (python-docx)
description: Generate a Word .docx file with cover page, results tables, and embedded figures from a single dict of study results. Saves about an hour per report and prevents copy-paste errors. Uses TNEI-style section structure but easily reskinned.

blocks.text: The pattern: keep a `results.json` (or pickle, or DB row) as the single source of truth. The script renders prose, tables, and figures into Word — no manual transcription. Re-run when the study is updated; output is byte-identical for unchanged data.

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Cm, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
import json

with open('results.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

doc = Document()

# ── Style defaults
style = doc.styles['Normal']
style.font.name = 'Calibri'
style.font.size = Pt(11)

# ── Cover page
title = doc.add_paragraph()
title.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
run = title.add_run(data['project'])
run.bold = True
run.font.size = Pt(28)
run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x29, 0x37)

subtitle = doc.add_paragraph()
subtitle.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
subtitle.add_run(f"Connection Study — {data['report_type']}\n\n")
subtitle.add_run(f"Client: {data['client']}\n")
subtitle.add_run(f"Project ref: {data['project_ref']}\n")
subtitle.add_run(f"Date: {data['date']}")

doc.add_page_break()

# ── 1. Executive summary
doc.add_heading('1.  Executive Summary', level=1)
doc.add_paragraph(data['executive_summary'])

# ── 2. Network description
doc.add_heading('2.  Network and Modelling Assumptions', level=1)
doc.add_paragraph(data['network_description'])

# Bullet list of assumptions
doc.add_heading('Key assumptions', level=2)
for a in data['assumptions']:
    doc.add_paragraph(a, style='List Bullet')

# ── 3. Load-flow results
doc.add_heading('3.  Load-Flow Results', level=1)
doc.add_paragraph('Bus voltages and line loadings under the base case are summarised below.')

# Bus voltages table
tbl = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=4)
tbl.style = 'Light Grid Accent 1'
hdr = tbl.rows[0].cells
hdr[0].text = 'Bus'
hdr[1].text = 'Voltage (pu)'
hdr[2].text = 'Voltage (kV)'
hdr[3].text = 'Status'
for bus in data['bus_results']:
    row = tbl.add_row().cells
    row[0].text = bus['name']
    row[1].text = f"{bus['Vmag_pu']:.4f}"
    row[2].text = f"{bus['Vmag_kV']:.2f}"
    row[3].text = bus['status']

# Embed voltage profile figure
doc.add_paragraph()
doc.add_picture('voltage-profile.png', width=Cm(15))
caption = doc.add_paragraph('Figure 1 — Bus voltage profile, base case.')
caption.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
caption.runs[0].italic = True

# ── 4. Fault levels
doc.add_heading('4.  Fault Level Summary', level=1)
doc.add_paragraph('Maximum fault currents per bus (worst-case across the four fault types):')

tbl = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=3)
tbl.style = 'Light Grid Accent 1'
hdr = tbl.rows[0].cells
hdr[0].text = 'Bus'
hdr[1].text = 'I_fault max (kA)'
hdr[2].text = 'Margin to breaker (%)'
for f in data['fault_results']:
    row = tbl.add_row().cells
    row[0].text = f['bus']
    row[1].text = f"{f['Imax_kA']:.2f}"
    row[2].text = f"{f['margin_pct']:.1f}%"

# ── 5. Conclusions
doc.add_heading('5.  Conclusions and Recommendations', level=1)
for c in data['conclusions']:
    doc.add_paragraph(c, style='List Bullet')

doc.save(f"{data['project_ref']}-connection-study.docx")
print(f"Wrote {data['project_ref']}-connection-study.docx")

Keep results.json as the contract between solver and report. The solver writes results.json; the report renderer reads it. This means you can swap solvers (PowerFactory CSV → Python script → in-house tool) without changing the report layout.

For company-style reports, save a docx 'template' with your house cover page, headers, and styles, then load it with `Document('template.docx')` instead of `Document()`. python-docx preserves all the existing styles and you only insert your dynamic content.

python-docx can't directly insert page numbers or auto-update Tables of Contents. The TOC will appear empty until someone opens the file in Word and presses F9 to refresh fields. A `LibreOffice --headless --convert-to docx` post-process can also force the refresh on a build server.
